narrative: The model estimated a 64% probability that you would fail the bar exam on the first attempt, meaning it judged failure more likely than success, and that is why your law school application was denied. The strongest factor was your third-year academic standing: your first-decile placement, compared with accepted students averaging near the sixth decile, pushed the prediction most strongly toward failure. Your LSAT score of 23.50, well below the accepted average of 37.18, was the second-strongest factor and also pushed toward failure. Your undergraduate GPA of 2.30, below the 3.23 average among accepted students, was the third most influential factor, but it worked in the opposite direction, shifting the prediction toward passing. Even so, the first two signals outweighed it. Gender and race were not used in this decision. To improve your chances, ask admissions for feedback, prepare for and consider retaking the LSAT, strengthen your academic record through additional coursework or relevant legal experience, and explain any extenuating circumstances. Reapply only after you can show meaningful improvement, and work with an admissions advisor to build a realistic plan.
